name: Eggplant Parmigiana
description: The Neapolitan Sunday ritual: fat rounds of fried eggplant layered with a slow tomato sauce, torn basil, and fior di latte mozzarella, then baked until the layers meld into something greater than the sum of their parts — bronzed on top, yielding within.

ingredients.note: Coarse salt (for drawing moisture from eggplant)
Olive oil or sunflower oil, for shallow frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
San Marzano tomatoes, hand-crushed (two 400 g tins)
Extra-virgin olive oil, for the sauce
Fior di latte mozzarella, torn or sliced 5 mm thick

name: Eggs Benedict Casserole
description: All the components of Eggs Benedict — toasted English muffin, Canadian bacon, egg — layered in a baking dish and baked ahead, then topped with easy blender hollandaise. Brunch for a crowd without the panic.

ingredients.note: English muffins, split and torn into pieces

name: Eggs Benedict
description: The Sunday-brunch apex — softly poached eggs draped over crisped Canadian bacon and toasted English muffin halves, drowned in a warm golden hollandaise sharpened with lemon. Three separate techniques — emulsion, poach, toast — synchronized into one showy plate.

ingredients.note: Clarified butter (warm); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Eggs en Cocotte
description: Eggs baked inside individual ramekins nestled in cream and herbs — each white just set, yolk still trembling and liquid, eaten by dragging toasted soldiers through the surface.

name: Egusi Stew
description: Ground melon seeds fried in a rich red palm oil base with Scotch bonnet pepper and crayfish, then simmered until they set into a thick, savory stew worthy of a feast — the mother of Nigerian soups.

ingredients.note: Beef (short rib or brisket, cut into 5 cm pieces)
Ground egusi (dried melon seeds, coarsely milled)
Pepper base: tomatoes, red bell peppers, Scotch bonnets, onion (blended raw)
Beef or chicken stock (or meat braising liquid); made up to 200 ml with boiling water
Fresh spinach or bitter leaf (roughly chopped)

name: Elote Callejero (Mexican Street Corn)
description: Corn charred on a comal or grill, then slathered with mayonnaise, rolled in crumbled Cotija cheese, dusted with chili, and finished with fresh lime — Mexico's greatest street snack.

name: Elote
description: Whole ears of corn blistered directly over an open flame until the kernels caramelize and char in spots, then rolled in crema, packed with cotija, dusted with chili powder, and finished with a squeeze of lime that sizzles against the hot surface.

name: Elotes
description: Charred whole ears of corn slathered in tangy Mexican crema, rolled in salty Cotija, dusted with chili powder, and hit with a squeeze of lime — every bite is simultaneously smoky, creamy, salty, acidic, and alive with heat.

name: Enchiladas Verdes
description: Corn tortillas, briefly fried and pulled through a bright, tangy tomatillo sauce, encase a filling of shredded chicken and emerge from the oven under a blanket of crema and queso fresco that softens the fire of the green chile.

name: Escalivada
description: Catalonia's great summer dish — eggplant, red peppers, and onion roasted whole over flame or in a scorching oven until the skins blacken and collapse, then peeled and torn into long sweet, smoky ribbons dressed with olive oil. The technique is as old as fire itself.

ingredients.note: Coarse sea salt and black pepper

name: Ethiopian Doro Wat
description: Chicken drumsticks and hard-boiled eggs braised deep into a caramelized onion and berbere stew — a dish of extraordinary depth built not from stock but from patience, red onion, and spice.

ingredients.note: Water or chicken stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Ethiopian Injera
description: A vast, sour teff crepe riddled with a thousand tiny eyes — the living gluten-free bread of Ethiopia that is simultaneously plate, utensil, and fermented foundation for every stew it holds.

name: Eton Mess
description: Smashed meringue, lightly crushed strawberries, and billowing whipped cream folded together at the last possible moment — deliberately imperfect and completely irresistible, a dessert whose name celebrates its own disorder.

name: Falafel
description: The Levantine street-corner standard — dried chickpeas never cooked, only soaked and ground raw with herbs and spice into a damp green rubble, then fried hard so the crust shatters into a craggy mahogany shell and the inside steams open soft, bright, and grassy.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Farinata Genovese
description: A thin, crackling chickpea-flour pancake from the Ligurian coast — blistered and gilt at the edges from a screaming-hot copper pan, custardy and golden within, needing nothing but black pepper and a patient oven.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Farro Risotto with Herbs and Parmesan
description: Pearled farro cooked risotto-style — ladle by ladle — until the ancient grain is tender but satisfyingly chewy, bound in a savory Parmigiano cream scented with thyme and finished with a proper mantecatura of cold butter.

ingredients.note: Vegetable or chicken stock, hot; made up to 600 ml with boiling water

name: Brown rice Risotto with Herbs and Parmesan (gluten-free)
description: Pearled brown rice cooked risotto-style — ladle by ladle — until the ancient grain is tender but satisfyingly chewy, bound in a savory Parmigiano cream scented with thyme and finished with a proper mantecatura of cold butter. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

ingredients.note: Vegetable or chicken stock, hot; made up to 600 ml with boiling water

name: Farro Salad
description: An Italian grain salad built on the nutty, chewy foundation of whole farro — tossed still warm with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, peppery arugula, sharp pecorino, and a lemon-olive oil dressing that soaks into every grain.

ingredients.note: Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Brown rice Salad (gluten-free)
description: An Italian grain salad built on the nutty, chewy foundation of whole brown rice — tossed still warm with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, peppery arugula, sharp pecorino, and a lemon-olive oil dressing that soaks into every grain. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

ingredients.note: Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Farrotto al Parmigiano
description: Farro risotto — pearled farro cooked risotto-style, ladleful by ladleful, until it reaches a creamy, gloriously al dente texture with more chew and nuttiness than Arborio could ever offer, finished with the classic mantecatura of cold butter and parmesan.

ingredients.note: Warm vegetable or chicken stock; made up to 1200 ml with boiling water

name: Farrotto al Parmigiano (gluten-free)
description: Brown rice risotto — pearled brown rice cooked risotto-style, ladleful by ladleful, until it reaches a creamy, gloriously al dente texture with more chew and nuttiness than Arborio could ever offer, finished with the classic mantecatura of cold butter and parmesan. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

ingredients.note: Warm vegetable or chicken stock; made up to 1200 ml with boiling water

name: Financier
description: A small rectangular cake with a crackling, caramelized crust that gives way to a moist, almond-scented interior perfumed with brown butter — the shell behaves like a biscuit, the center like a warm frangipane. Created by Parisian pastry chefs for bankers who couldn't afford to stain their cuffs.

name: Financiers
description: Small bar-shaped almond cakes made with browned butter and almond flour, producing a chewy, moist interior and a nutty, caramelized crust — the perfect one-bite teatime classic.

name: Beer-Battered Fish and Chips
description: Thick fillets of cod sheathed in a shattering, golden-crisp beer batter that balloons and blisters in the hot fat — while inside, the fish steams to a tender, sweet flake — served with malt-vinegar-doused fat chips that are fluffy within and bronzed without.

ingredients.note: Thick cod fillets (skin removed), 200 g each
Maris Piper or King Edward potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm batons
Beef dripping or neutral frying oil (enough to deep fry); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Gluten-free beer-Battered Fish and Chips (gluten-free)
description: Thick fillets of cod sheathed in a shattering, golden-crisp gluten-free beer batter that balloons and blisters in the hot fat — while inside, the fish steams to a tender, sweet flake — served with cider-vinegar-doused fat chips that are fluffy within and bronzed without. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free beer instead of beer or ale.

ingredients.note: Thick cod fillets (skin removed), 200 g each
instead of Ice-cold lager or pale ale
Maris Piper or King Edward potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm batons
Beef dripping or neutral frying oil (enough to deep fry); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Flamiche aux Poireaux
description: A rich, open-faced tart of slowly stewed leeks and cream in a crisp pâte brisée shell — simple, warming, and deeply savory, the great leek tart of northern France.

name: Flamiche aux Poireaux (gluten-free)
description: A rich, open-faced tart of slowly stewed leeks and cream in a crisp pâte brisée shell — simple, warming, and deeply savory, the great leek tart of northern France. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Flan de Leche
description: A trembling, silken custard baked in a water bath until it barely sets, then inverted so that the bittersweet caramel pooled in the base flows down its sides in amber rivulets. The contrast between the dark, slightly bitter caramel and the pale, sweetly eggy custard beneath is one of the most elegant flavour contrasts in the Spanish kitchen.

name: Freekeh Pilaf with Caramelized Onions
description: Whole freekeh — wheat harvested green and roasted over open fires — simmered in spiced broth until it delivers its signature campfire smokiness, buried under a crown of slow-caramelized onions that collapse into strands of dark, sweet gold.

ingredients.note: Vegetable or chicken stock; made up to 550 ml with boiling water
Large yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
Toasted pine nuts or slivered almonds
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Brown rice Pilaf with Caramelized Onions (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Whole brown rice — brown rice harvested green and roasted over open fires — simmered in spiced broth until it delivers its signature campfire smokiness, buried under a crown of slow-caramelized onions that collapse into strands of dark, sweet gold. This gluten- & nut-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh, sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: instead of Whole freekeh (green roasted wheat)
Vegetable or chicken stock; made up to 550 ml with boiling water
Large yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
instead of Toasted pine nuts or slivered almonds
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: French Rolled Omelette
description: A pale, unmarked envelope of barely set curds — the Escoffier benchmark where technique replaces seasoning and the pan does half the thinking.

name: Provençal Ratatouille
description: Summer's abundance — eggplant, zucchini, tomato, and pepper — slow-roasted with olive oil and thyme until each vegetable concentrates into a jewel-bright, silky confit that no longer tastes of individual parts.

ingredients.note: Red bell pepper, cut into 2cm pieces

name: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken
description: Bone-in chicken soaked long and slow in seasoned buttermilk until the acid tenderises every fibre, then dredged in spiced flour and fried in a cast-iron skillet in shallow lard until the crust shatters like a cracker and the interior runs with its own juice.

ingredients.note: Bone-in chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts, wings)
Lard for frying (enough for 4 cm depth in skillet); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken (gluten-free)
description: Bone-in chicken soaked long and slow in seasoned buttermilk until the acid tenderises every fibre, then dredged in spiced gluten-free flour and fried in a cast-iron skillet in shallow lard until the crust shatters like a cracker and the interior runs with its own juice. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Bone-in chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts, wings)
Lard for frying (enough for 4 cm depth in skillet); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Italian Frittata
description: A thick, golden disc of eggs — set at the edges, custardy at the heart — studded with whatever the season offers, finished in the oven until the top blooms in faint bronze islands.

name: Frumenty
description: The great wheat pottage of the medieval table — cracked wheat soaked and seethed until it bursts and goes glutinous, then enriched with milk, gilded with saffron, and bound at the last with egg yolks into a thick, golden, spoon-coating porridge served beside venison or fish.

ingredients.note: Whole wheat berries, cracked (bulgur or cracked wheat)

name: Frumenty (gluten-free)
description: The great brown rice pottage of the medieval table — brown rice soaked and seethed until it bursts and goes glutinous, then enriched with milk, gilded with saffron, and bound at the last with egg yolks into a thick, golden, spoon-coating porridge served beside venison or fish. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

ingredients.note: instead of Whole wheat berries, cracked (bulgur or cracked wheat)

name: Gambas al Ajillo
description: Spain's most seductive tapa — prawns seared in an inferno of olive oil, garlic, and dried chile until the shells spit and sizzle, eaten straight from the clay cazuela with torn gluten-free bread to drag through the garlicky oil.

ingredients.note: Dried guindilla peppers or red chile

name: Garlic Butter Shrimp with Lemony Pea Rice
description: Plump shrimp seared hard and fast, then rolled through a sizzling pan of butter, sliced garlic and lemon, spooned with all their buttery juices over fluffy stock-cooked rice studded with sweet green peas.

ingredients.note: Long-grain white rice, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 550 ml with boiling water
Large shrimp (16–20 per lb), peeled and deveined, tails on or off

name: Gazpacho Andaluz
description: Andalusia's legendary chilled raw tomato soup — peak-season tomatoes blended with stale bread, cucumber, pepper, sherry vinegar, and olive oil into a silky, ice-cold soup that pours like velvet.

ingredients.note: Ripe plum tomatoes, cored and roughly chopped
Green bell pepper, seeded and roughly chopped
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish

name: Gazpacho Andaluz (gluten-free)
description: Andalusia's legendary chilled raw tomato soup — peak-season tomatoes blended with gluten-free bread, cucumber, pepper, sherry vinegar, and olive oil into a silky, ice-cold soup that pours like velvet. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: Ripe plum tomatoes, cored and roughly chopped
Green bell pepper, seeded and roughly chopped
instead of Stale white bread, crusts removed
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish

name: Ginger Chicken & Rice Soup
description: A clear, golden broth steeped with a fistful of sliced ginger, scallion, and garlic, filled with tender pulled chicken, soft rice, and napa cabbage — gentle, warming, and pointed up with fish sauce and white pepper.
origin: East and Southeast Asian home kitchen

ingredients.note: Scallions, whites and greens separated, greens thinly sliced
Napa cabbage, cut into 2 cm ribbons

name: Ginger-Scallion Pork Noodles with Bok Choy
description: Chewy wheat noodles tossed with browned, soy-glazed ground pork, tender bok choy, and a sizzling ginger-scallion oil that tastes grassy, sharp and fragrant all at once.

ingredients.note: Wheat noodles, dried (lo mein, ramen-style or thin udon)
Baby bok choy, quartered lengthwise and washed
Rice vinegar or Chinkiang black vinegar

name: Ginger-Scallion Pork Noodles with Bok Choy (gluten-free)
description: Chewy rice noodles tossed with browned, soy-glazed ground pork, tender bok choy, and a sizzling ginger-scallion oil that tastes grassy, sharp and fragrant all at once. This gluten-free version uses rice noodles instead of egg noodles, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, rice vinegar instead of chinese black vinegar.

ingredients.note: instead of Wheat noodles, dried (lo mein, ramen-style or thin udon)
Baby bok choy, quartered lengthwise and washed
instead of Rice vinegar or Chinkiang black vinegar

name: Gnocchi al Burro e Salvia
description: Potato gnocchi made right have the texture of clouds condensed into something you can hold — impossibly light, barely structured, yielding at the touch of a fork. Brown the butter to hazelnut, fry sage leaves until they shatter, and the whole thing becomes northern Italian winter in a bowl.

ingredients.note: Floury potatoes, such as Russet or King Edward (about 700g before baking)

name: Gluten-free gnocchi al Burro e Salvia (gluten-free)
description: Potato gnocchi made right have the texture of clouds condensed into something you can hold — impossibly light, barely structured, yielding at the touch of a fork. Brown the butter to hazelnut, fry sage leaves until they shatter, and the whole thing becomes northern Italian winter in a bowl. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Floury potatoes, such as Russet or King Edward (about 700g before baking)
instead of 00 flour (plus more for the bench)

name: Gluten-free gnocchi di Patate
description: Pillowy potato dumplings from the Veneto — baked starchy potatoes riced while still hot and worked with just enough gluten-free flour to hold together, shaped into ridged cushions that cook in seconds and dissolve on the tongue.

ingredients.note: Floury potatoes (Russet or King Edward), unpeeled
Unsalted butter and fresh sage leaves, for serving

name: Potato Gnocchi
description: Cloud-light pillow-dumplings made from still-warm baked potato, just enough flour, and a single egg — the Italian grandmother's paradox: the less you work the dough, the better the gnocchi. One extra gram of flour is the difference between a dumpling and a torpedo.

ingredients.note: Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes (floury variety)

name: Potato Gnocchi (gluten-free)
description: Cloud-light pillow-dumplings made from still-warm baked potato, just enough gluten-free flour, and a single egg — the Italian grandmother's paradox: the less you work the dough, the better the gluten-free gnocchi. One extra gram of flour is the difference between a dumpling and a torpedo. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes (floury variety)
instead of All-purpose flour (plus extra for bench)

name: Gratin Dauphinois
description: Paper-thin potato slices layered in garlicked cream and baked until the top is deeply golden and bubbling while the interior becomes a single, unified, silky mass — the most indulgent thing you can do with a potato.

ingredients.note: Floury potatoes (Russet or Maris Piper, peeled)
Garlic cloves (1 halved for rubbing, 2 minced)

name: Scandinavian Gravlax
description: Salmon cured raw in equal parts salt and sugar with masses of fresh dill — no heat, no smoke, just chemistry and time turning the flesh translucent and silken over two days.

ingredients.note: Coarse sea salt (not table salt, not iodised)

name: Greek Baked Sea Bass (Lavraki Plaki)
description: A whole sea bass laid on a bed of tomatoes, onions, and potatoes, drowned in olive oil and white wine, and baked low and slow until everything is silky and the fish falls from the bone at a glance.

ingredients.note: Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper

name: Galaktoboureko
description: Shatteringly crisp filo leaves encasing a thick, trembling vanilla semolina custard, drenched at the moment of emergence from the oven with cold lemon-scented syrup so it hisses and absorbs.

name: Gigantes Plaki
description: Enormous white butter beans baked low and slow in a rich tomato sauce with olive oil, celery, and sweet onion until their skins split and their interiors become creamy and yielding — the sauce reducing to a thick, tomatoey glaze that the beans absorb like sponges.

ingredients.note: Dried gigantes beans (giant white beans), soaked overnight
Water or vegetable stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
description: Pounded and bruised in a clay mortar, shredded green papaya transforms into a vivid, dripping tangle where every strand carries sour lime, salty fish sauce, and enough chili heat to turn the tips of your ears red.

ingredients.note: Thai bird's eye chilies (2-5, adjust to tolerance)
Dried shrimp (kung haeng) — optional for Isan style
Long beans or green beans, cut into 3cm pieces

name: Grilled Asparagus with Lemon and Parmesan
description: Thick asparagus spears rolled in olive oil and grilled at high heat until the tips blister to a charred, crispy fringe and the stalks take on sweet, smoky char while remaining tender enough to snap cleanly — finished with bright lemon and nutty shaved parmesan.

ingredients.note: Thick asparagus spears, woody ends snapped off

name: Grilled Lamb Chops
description: Rosemary-garlic marinated lamb loin chops seared over high heat to a rosé center and charred perimeter, carved and served in a pool of their own resting juices.

ingredients.note: Lamb loin chops (2–3 cm thick, frenched)

name: Mediterranean Grilled Octopus
description: A whole octopus slow-poached in a wine-and-herb court until the tentacles yield like braised beef, then scorched on a screaming grill until the suckers blister and char — finished with bright lemon, capers, flat-leaf parsley, and a flood of grassy olive oil.

ingredients.note: Whole octopus, cleaned (mantle and beak removed)

name: Grilled Whole Branzino
description: A whole European sea bass seasoned simply with olive oil, lemon, and herbs, grilled over fierce heat until the skin blisters and shatters and the sweet flesh inside steams in its own juices — Mediterranean cooking at its most honest and dramatic.

ingredients.note: Whole branzino (European sea bass), cleaned and scaled, about 500g each
Lemon, half for juice, half sliced thin

name: Mediterranean Grilled Whole Fish
description: A whole sea bass or bream scored through its skin and filled with lemon slices, herbs, and garlic, then grilled over open coals until the skin blisters and crisps away from the flesh and the flesh itself sweats its juices onto the grate below. The Greek fisherman's answer to technique: simplicity, fire, and time.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bass or sea bream (400–500 g each), scaled and gutted

name: Gulab Jamun
description: Milk-solid dumplings fried to mahogany, then soaked in cardamom-rosewater syrup until swollen, sticky, and deeply fragrant — the most beloved Indian sweet, at once crisp and yielding, the syrup forcing its way to the very centre during the long soak.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil or ghee for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Gulab Jamun (gluten-free)
description: Milk-solid dumplings fried to mahogany, then soaked in cardamom-rosewater syrup until swollen, sticky, and deeply fragrant — the most beloved Indian sweet, at once crisp and yielding, the syrup forcing its way to the very centre during the long soak. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil or ghee for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Gyoza — Pan-Fried Pork & Cabbage Dumplings
description: Thin-skinned crescents of pork and cabbage that are steamed and then seared in a single unbroken maneuver, producing a crisp caramelized bottom and a taut, translucent top. They release from the pan in one dramatic sheet.

name: Halloumi Grain Bowls
description: Nutty, chewy farro tossed in a sharp lemon-oregano dressing with crisp cucumber, sweet tomatoes, and briny olives, topped with slabs of halloumi seared to a squeaky golden crust.

name: Halloumi Grain Bowls (gluten-free)
description: Nutty, chewy brown rice tossed in a sharp lemon-oregano dressing with crisp cucumber, sweet tomatoes, and briny olives, topped with slabs of halloumi seared to a squeaky golden crust. This gluten-free version uses brown rice instead of farro or freekeh.

name: Haricots Verts Amandine
description: Tender-crisp French green beans blanched to vivid green and finished in foamy browned butter scattered with toasted slivered almonds — the essence of classical French elegance.

ingredients.note: Haricots verts (French green beans), stem ends trimmed

name: Haricots Verts Amandine (nut-free)
description: Tender-crisp French green beans blanched to vivid green and finished in foamy browned butter scattered with sunflower seeds — the essence of classical French elegance. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

ingredients.note: Haricots verts (French green beans), stem ends trimmed

name: Sheet-Pan Harissa Chicken with Chickpeas and Cauliflower
description: Chicken thighs rubbed in smoky, brick-red harissa roast over chickpeas that turn crackly at the edges and cauliflower that sweetens and browns in the spiced drippings, all cooled off with a spoonful of lemony yogurt.

ingredients.note: Fresh cilantro or parsley, roughly chopped

name: Herb-Roasted Leg of Lamb
description: A bone-in leg of lamb studded with garlic, coated in a Dijon-herb crust, and roasted until the fat renders golden and the center stays a vivid rose-pink.

ingredients.note: Bone-in leg of lamb (2–2.5 kg, trimmed of excess fat)
Garlic cloves, peeled and cut into thin slivers
Extra-virgin olive oil; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Dry white wine or water (for roasting pan)
Anchovy fillets in oil (optional, flavor deepener)

name: Medovik Honey Cake
description: The beloved Russian layered cake of thin, golden, honey-kissed sponge rounds, each one softened overnight under the weight of a tangy sour cream frosting that melts the layers into a single, harmonious, meltingly tender whole.

name: Medovik Honey Cake (gluten-free)
description: The beloved Russian layered cake of thin, golden, honey-kissed sponge rounds, each one softened overnight under the weight of a tangy sour cream frosting that melts the layers into a single, harmonious, meltingly tender whole. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Honeycomb Toffee (Cinder Toffee)
description: Sugar and golden syrup cooked to the hard-crack stage, then dramatically aerated by a single teaspoon of baking soda that transforms molten candy into a volcanic, rising foam of caramel glass — crunchy, airy, and dangerously addictive, especially when shattered and dipped in dark chocolate.

name: Hong Kong Egg Tarts (Dan Tat)
description: A shortcrust shell made with lard shatters at the tooth like a cream cracker, cradling a smooth, barely-set vanilla egg custard that trembles when the plate is moved — the custard surface is completely smooth, not pocked, and tastes clean, faintly sweet, and deeply eggy. These are the reason Cantonese cha chaan teng (tea houses) exist.

name: Hong Kong Egg Tarts (Dan Tat) (gluten-free)
description: A shortcrust shell made with lard shatters at the tooth like a cream cracker, cradling a smooth, barely-set vanilla egg custard that trembles when the plate is moved — the custard surface is completely smooth, not pocked, and tastes clean, faintly sweet, and deeply eggy. These are the reason Cantonese cha chaan teng (tea houses) exist. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Hoppin' John
description: Black-eyed peas braised low and slow with a smoked ham hock, onion, and rice in their own broth — the dish of luck and prosperity eaten on New Year's Day across the American South, rooted in the Gullah Geechee food traditions of the Lowcountry.

ingredients.note: Smoked ham hock or thick-cut bacon

name: Imam Bayıldı
description: Whole eggplants slit lengthwise and filled with a slow-cooked melange of onion, tomato, garlic, and olive oil, then braised in more olive oil until the eggplant walls collapse into translucent silk — the dish whose name means 'the imam fainted,' allegedly from the extravagance of the oil.

ingredients.note: Kosher salt, black pepper, and a pinch of sugar

name: Isicia Omentata
description: Rome's answer to the burger, lifted straight from Apicius: minced beef pounded with pepper and pine nuts, soused with salty garum and a splash of wine, then wrapped in lacy caul fat that bastes the patty as it sears into a crisp, savoury shell. Smoky, funky, and unmistakably ancient.

ingredients.note: Stale bread soaked in wine (squeezed dry)

name: Isicia Omentata (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Rome's answer to the burger, lifted straight from Apicius: minced beef pounded with pepper and sunflower seeds, soused with salty garum and a splash of wine, then wrapped in lacy caul fat that bastes the patty as it sears into a crisp, savoury shell. Smoky, funky, and unmistakably ancient. This gluten- & nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts, gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: instead of Toasted pine nuts (lightly crushed)
instead of Stale bread soaked in wine (squeezed dry)

name: Italian Acqua Pazza
description: Fish poached in 'crazy water' — a bubbling broth of cherry tomatoes, white wine, and olive oil that drives itself to a boil in the pan, perfuming the fish with the sea breeze of the southern Italian coast.

ingredients.note: Whole fish (sea bream, snapper, or sea bass), cleaned

name: Japanese Cotton Cheesecake
description: A cake that trembles like set custard, its surface burnished to deep amber, its crumb so aerated it yields to a spoon like foam — a soufflé's lightness married to cream cheese's gentle tang, impossibly sustained.

name: Japanese Cotton Cheesecake (gluten-free)
description: A cake that trembles like set custard, its surface burnished to deep amber, its crumb so aerated it yields to a spoon like foam — a soufflé's lightness married to cream cheese's gentle tang, impossibly sustained. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Japanese Curry
description: The most comforting dish in the Japanese home kitchen: golden-brown chicken and sweet potato disappearing into a glossy, deeply spiced sauce that straddles the line between curry and gravy — warming, mildly sweet, and built for bowls of short-grain rice on cold evenings.

ingredients.note: Chicken thigh, bone-in or boneless (cut into large chunks)
Japanese curry roux blocks (S&B Golden Curry or similar)
Water or chicken stock; made up to 400 ml with boiling water
